annotation_description: Playing a Mountain instead of Rockface Village on turn 1 when casting a creature spell (Hired Claw). Rockface Village's creature-only red mana is sufficient for Hired Claw, and playing it first preserves unrestricted Mountains for later non-creature spells. Additionally, Rockface Village has a pump ability for Lizards like Hired Claw that becomes available sooner.

Gem3P Villain has three lands in hand (Hallowed Fountain, Island, Plains) and only one land on the battlefield (Restless Anchorage). It's turn 2 and they need to make their land drop to curve toward Day of Judgment on turn 4 or No More Lies on turn 2. By not playing a land, they fall behind on mana development. Playing Hallowed Fountain (paying 2 life to have it enter untapped) would give them access to WU to hold up No More Lies this turn, which is particularly important since the opponent has a Mountain and could deploy threats.

Playing Island instead of Plains with a hand containing Elspeth (3WW) and Day of Judgment (2WW) is slightly suboptimal. Playing Plains first maximizes white mana available on turn 4, which matters if they draw a 4th land and need to cast Day of Judgment (2WW), or if they need to activate Restless Anchorage (1WU) while also holding up No More Lies. Plains-first keeps more options open.

Villain had an unplayed Island (or Fountainport) in hand. By playing a land first (making 6 lands), they could activate Restless Anchorage for {1}{W}{U} and still have 3 lands untapped - enough to hold up No More Lies ({W}{U}). Instead they passed, missing 2 damage and a Map token for free.

Declined to counter Lightning Strike with No More Lies when the opponent had only 1 land untapped (Rockface Village) and couldn't pay the {3} tax. The counter would have been guaranteed to exile the spell, saving 3 damage. While at 20 life 3 damage isn't critical, No More Lies is a cheap counterspell being used on a cheap spell - it's trading evenly on mana. However, saving the counter for a more impactful threat (like Nova Hellkite or Hexing Squelcher) is a reasonable argument, especially since Villain has Day of Judgment and Elspeth as powerful plays coming up. The decision is debatable but taking 3 unnecessary damage when you have a guaranteed counter available is worth questioning.

Villain passed with 5 mana available and Elspeth in hand while the opponent has no creatures, no board presence, and is nearly tapped out (only 1 untapped land producing colorless/conditional R). This wastes a prime window to deploy Elspeth safely. Elspeth would immediately create 2 tokens (due to doubling passive) and go to 6 loyalty, making it very difficult for the opponent to answer next turn even with a Lightning Strike (only 3 damage vs 6 loyalty).

Passed the turn without casting Elspeth, Storm Slayer when the opponent has zero creatures on board and only 1 untapped land (Rockface Village). Elspeth would immediately create 2 soldier tokens (doubled by her static ability) with +1, going to 6 loyalty, establishing a dominant board position against an opponent with no pressure and limited resources.

Casting Shock to face for 2 damage instead of deploying Hexing Squelcher. Hexing Squelcher can't be countered (safe against the UW opponent's likely countermagic), puts a 2/2 body on board for pressure, and crucially makes all spells uncounterable - enabling Nova Hellkite to land safely next turn through the opponent's No More Lies or other counters.

Gem3P Villain declined to counter a Shock with No More Lies available. Shock deals 2 damage and at 17 life this matters, but more importantly, the opponent has very few cards and resources - countering their spells denies them tempo and card advantage. The opponent likely targeted Gem3P Villain directly (bringing them to 15) or could be targeting something relevant. With No More Lies costing only WU (which Gem3P has available via Hallowed Fountain + Island), there's little reason not to counter it. The 3 mana tax from No More Lies would almost certainly counter Shock since the opponent has 4 lands tapped (postcombat main). Additionally, letting damage through when you're already at 17 life against a red aggro deck is risky, especially when you have a 5-mana Elspeth you want to deploy next turn.

Activating Fountainport to create a 1/1 Fish token on their own postcombat main phase costs 3 mana + tap Fountainport + 1 life, leaving only 1 untapped land. This sacrifices the ability to hold up No More Lies (WU) against the opponent's next turn threats. A 1/1 token provides minimal value compared to keeping countermagic available when the opponent has 5 cards in hand. Additionally, they haven't played their Island from hand yet - they should play the land first if they want to maximize options.

With no opposing creatures on board and the opponent having only 4 mana available (limited to burn spells as interaction), this was likely the best window to deploy Elspeth, Storm Slayer. On an empty board, Elspeth immediately +1s to 6 loyalty with a 1/1 soldier (doubled to two 1/1s), and the opponent's burn (at most Lightning Strike for 3 + Shock for 2 = 5 damage to planeswalker) likely can't kill her in one turn, especially through blockers. Passing to hold up No More Lies is defensible but overly conservative when the opponent's threat density is limited by their 4 available mana.

Gem3P Villain passed their entire turn without casting Elspeth, Storm Slayer on a completely empty opposing board. With 5 available mana (Plains, Hallowed Fountain for WW, plus Island, Fountainport, Restless Anchorage for generic), Elspeth could be deployed immediately, going to 6 loyalty with +1 and creating 2 soldier tokens (due to the doubling static). The opponent has no creatures and only 4 lands, making this an ideal window. Additionally, Restless Anchorage could have been animated to attack as a 2/3 flyer.

Gem3P Villain declined to activate Restless Anchorage during combat. The opponent has no untapped mana (only one tapped Mountain and three untapped Mountains plus Rockface Village), but their burn spells cost 1R (Shock) or 1R (Lightning Strike) — both already in the graveyard. With no cards in the opponent's hand that we know threaten the land, and the opponent's board being empty of creatures, attacking for 2 flying damage and creating a Map token (which can later be sacrificed for value via Fountainport's draw ability) is essentially free. The risk of losing Restless Anchorage to removal is minimal since the opponent's known burn is in the graveyard, and 2 damage chips away at the opponent's life total while generating incremental value.

With all opponent lands tapped (no countermagic threat), casting Nova Hellkite (4/5 flying haste) would be stronger. It can immediately attack Elspeth for 4 damage (5→1) while leaving a major threat on board, compared to Lightning Strike which deals only 3 damage and leaves less board presence. The opponent being fully tapped out makes this the ideal window to resolve the most impactful threat.

With all of Villain's lands tapped (no counterspell risk), Hexing Squelcher's anti-counter ability is irrelevant this turn. By playing Mountain from hand first, Libby would have exactly 5 mana remaining after Lightning Strike (which is on the stack) to cast Nova Hellkite - a 4/5 flying haste creature that would deal 4 combat damage plus 1 ETB damage, representing far more pressure against a 15-life opponent.

Opponent has no creatures and is nearly tapped out (only 1 untapped Mountain). This was an opportunity to animate Restless Anchorage (paying {1}{W}{U}) and attack for 2 damage plus a Map token. While this uses mana that could hold up No More Lies, the opponent can only cast 1-mana spells with their available mana, making the counterspell less valuable this turn cycle.

Day of Judgment was cast when the opponent had zero creatures on the battlefield. This destroys only Gem3P's own soldier tokens from Elspeth while wasting a powerful board wipe that could have been saved for when the opponent deploys threats. The opponent has burn spells in graveyard and Mountains, suggesting aggressive creatures could come later.

MiniMx Libby played a Mountain before casting Nova Hellkite. They already have 5 mountains (4 Mountain + 1 Rockface Village) which is exactly enough to cast Nova Hellkite (3RR) using Warp (2R) or normal cost. Playing the land first is fine for mana, but the real issue is that they chose to play Mountain instead of casting Nova Hellkite. With Elspeth at 5 loyalty on the opponent's board (which creates tokens doubled and can destroy creatures), getting a hasty 4/5 flyer on board immediately is critical. Nova Hellkite with haste can attack Elspeth for 4 damage (bringing her to 1 loyalty) or hit the opponent's face. The opponent has 13 life and MiniMx has 2 Nova Hellkites and a Lightning Strike in hand (3+4+4 = 11 damage potential over upcoming turns). Every turn Elspeth stays alive, the opponent gains more advantage through doubled tokens and +1/+1 counters. Playing Mountain and passing without casting Nova Hellkite would waste a critical turn. However, looking more carefully - this is just the land drop decision, and they may still cast Nova Hellkite after playing the land. Playing the land first before casting spells is actually correct sequencing. But wait - they already had 5 lands (4 Mountains + 1 Rockface Village), which gives them exactly 5 mana for Nova Hellkite's {3}{R}{R} cost. The 6th land doesn't help cast anything additional this turn. The sequencing of land before spell is fine and standard practice. Actually, this is just playing a land - they can still cast Nova Hellkite this turn. This isn't a blunder at all since playing land before spells is correct sequencing.

Casting Nova Hellkite at full cost into Elspeth, Storm Slayer at 5 loyalty. Elspeth can simply use her -3 to destroy Nova Hellkite (MV 5 >= 3) next turn, effectively trading a premium threat for a planeswalker activation that still leaves Elspeth alive at 2 loyalty. Meanwhile, a Warp Hellkite + Lightning Strike line would kill Elspeth entirely.

Nova Hellkite (a 4/5 flying haste creature) is on the stack and Gem3P Villain has No More Lies in hand with the mana to cast it (Hallowed Fountain + Plains are untapped, providing W and U). At 13 life facing an aggressive red deck that has already burned them with Lightning Strikes and Shocks, letting a 4/5 flying haste creature resolve is devastating. Nova Hellkite will deal 1 damage to a creature on ETB and then attack for 4 in the air immediately, putting Gem3P Villain to 9 life or lower. With the opponent having cards in hand that are likely more burn spells, this could easily be lethal. Elspeth's soldier tokens can't block a flyer effectively. This is a must-counter threat.

Opponent has only 1 untapped Mountain, making it extremely unlikely they cast anything meaningful. Gem3P Villain could have used Fountainport to create a Fish token (doubled to 2 by Elspeth's static ability) for future chump blocking or card draw via Fountainport's sacrifice ability, instead of holding up mana for No More Lies against an opponent who can't cast anything significant.

Gem3P Villain is at 9 life facing a Nova Hellkite (4/5 flying haste) that will untap next turn. The opponent has 6 lands (one untapped Mountain) and has already cast Lightning Strike x2 and Shock from the graveyard, meaning burn spells are a real threat. Day of Judgment would destroy the Nova Hellkite and any other creatures cleanly, while Elspeth survives as a planeswalker. Instead, they used Elspeth's +1 to create a soldier token, which doesn't address the 4-damage flying threat that will attack next turn. The soldier tokens will also die to Day of Judgment if cast later, wasting the token creation. At 9 life, taking 4 from Hellkite puts them to 5, well within burn range (Lightning Strike = 3, Shock = 2). They should cast Day of Judgment immediately to remove the Hellkite, then use Elspeth's +1 to start rebuilding.

The player's reasoning correctly identified that Get Lost on Nova Hellkite is superior to Day of Judgment (preserving their 5 Soldier tokens while removing the threat), but then they just played Island instead of casting Get Lost. Nova Hellkite is a 4/5 flying haste creature that already attacked once, and leaving it alive means it can attack again next turn for 4 damage when the player is at only 9 life. The opponent has 5 tapped Mountains but will untap them, potentially having burn spells to finish the game. Playing the land first is fine but not casting Get Lost afterward wastes the opportunity to remove the immediate lethal threat.

Gem3P Villain plans to use Get Lost on Nova Hellkite when Elspeth's -3 ability could destroy it (MV 5 >= 3) without spending a card from hand and without giving the opponent two Map tokens. Get Lost should be saved for threats Elspeth can't handle.

Passed with mana available to activate Fountainport while still holding up No More Lies. With Elspeth's token-doubling passive, activating Fountainport to create a Fish token (getting 2 due to Elspeth) or a Treasure token (getting 2) would provide value. After tapping Fountainport + 2 other lands, Restless Anchorage + Hallowed Fountain or Plains still provide WU for No More Lies.

There is a Lightning Strike on the stack targeting Gem3P Villain (who is at 9 life). Gem3P Villain has No More Lies in hand and the mana to cast it (Hallowed Fountain for W, Plains for U or other available lands). Lightning Strike dealing 3 damage would put them to 6 life, which is very dangerous given the opponent has burn spells in their graveyard and likely more in their deck. No More Lies would counter it unless the opponent pays 3 additional mana, which they likely can't afford mid-combat. Letting 3 damage resolve when you have a counterspell available at 9 life is a significant mistake.

Opponent is completely tapped out with no creatures on board. Restless Anchorage could have been activated to attack as a 2/3 flyer for 2 damage plus generating a Map token, with zero risk since opponent has no blockers and no mana to respond.
Activated Elspeth's 0 ability with zero creatures on the battlefield, resulting in no effect whatsoever. The +1/+1 counters and flying were granted to nothing.

Gem3P Villain passed priority during their own combat phase without activating Restless Anchorage to attack as a 2/3 flyer. The opponent is at 10 life with no creatures to block. Activating Anchorage for {1}{W}{U} would deal 2 damage and create a Map token, while still leaving enough mana to hold up No More Lies for defensive purposes.

Casting Nova Hellkite for full cost (3RR) instead of Warp cost (2R) when the opponent has Elspeth's -3 to destroy it before next combat anyway. Both lines deliver the same 5 damage (1 ETB + 4 haste attack), but Warp saves 2 mana and loses less value if countered by the opponent's open UW mana.

Should play Soulstone Sanctuary (free land drop) before casting Nova Hellkite. Playing the land first costs nothing and provides an additional mana source plus a future 3/3 vigilance creature option, which matters when at 3 life.
